newsitem.title: DUBAI: BRITISH TRADE WITH GULF UP 20 PCT IN JAN-NOV 96.
newsitem.headline: BRITISH TRADE WITH GULF UP 20 PCT IN JAN-NOV 96.

text.p: Britain's trade with the six Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) states rose by more than 20 percent in the first eleven months of 1996 to 5.93 billion stg on the same period in 1995.

"These encouraging business trends will remind British business that the GCC is a key international partner," said Richard Parry, head of export promotions for the Arabian peninsula at the Department of Trade and Industry, in a statement.
British exports to the region rose 22 percent to nearly 4.59 billion stg from 3.76 billion stg in January-November 1995.
British imports from the GCC -- which is made up of Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Bahrain, Qatar, United Arab Emirates and Oman -- rose 16 percent to 1.34 billion pounds in the period.
The statement said exports to Saudi Arabia rose 35 percent in the first 11 months of 1996 to almost 2.03 billion stg.
Overall trade with Qatar increased by nearly 27 percent, the statement said, without giving a figure.
